assumptions: One class of 24 in 6 groups. For reusable items the quantity to hold is the largest single-week figure, not the sum of the weeks; consumables add up across weeks.
Where an item is marked 'both' but Plan A and Plan B need different amounts, the uses row gives the larger figure and the note gives each plan's figure.

Items prepared before a lesson are listed under that lesson's week. Language support pack and Before Week 1 items are listed under Week 1. The Weeks 7 to 8 strip trial is listed under Week 5 (Plan A may run it in Week 6).

Trial batch: the Week 7 kit card says freeze three plain trial strips and test them (the Teacher Guide Week 5 row and the outline say two; the kit card wins). The Week 8 kit card also wants 2 spare plain strips from the trial batch, so 5 trial strips are assumed (3 tested, 2 kept). Trial flour and salt (30 g and 35 g) are scaled from the batch recipe for about 90 g of dough.
Week 8 Plan A: up to two groups do the melting test (class project board rule), so strength-rig kit is counted for all 6 groups (needed if every group chooses strength) and melting kit for 2 groups.
The Week 8 teacher demo rig is costed from the rig diagram: two stacks of three books, 1 carrier bag, 1 hanger string, 1 bucket. The trial in Week 5 or 6 uses one more rig of the same kind.

Fibre amounts are upper limits for one class, based on 9 strips per group with 3 of them controls (no fibre): sawdust up to about 30 g; tissue, shredded paper and cotton wool up to about 12 g each; up to 36 fibre portions. The real amounts depend on the approved plans. If the trial calls for thinner 3 to 4 mm strips, the fibre doses drop (0.4 g per strip for fibre type; 0, 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6 g for amount), and so does the water (8 ml) or dough (12 g).

Card weight: 160 gsm is specified only for the spinner templates. The same card is assumed for the other card prints (footprint cards, question sort cards, voting cards, question cards, certificates).
Week 4 spinner card: 9 reserve sheets come from the Week 3 print spec. The Week 4 kit card puts only 3 on the teacher desk.

Plain-paper printables are left to reprographics and not listed: skills checks, surveys, checkpoints, worksheets, exit tickets, kit cards, odd-one-out cards, Bar or line? cards, Galileo A4 copies, sample labels, A4 pooling sheets, panel cards, talk frame cards, self-assessment slips, peer feedback slips, run sheet, talk record, gallery walk signs, sentence-frame posters and card sets. The outline's design brief says kit cards are 'laminated if possible', but no Year 7 file asks for it, so no pouches are listed for them.

The Scientist's Logbook and My Science Dictionary are plain-paper booklets. They are listed because the prep calendar names them as separate print jobs (booklets made up and stapled), not because they need special stock.
Lamination assumes the school has a laminator. Role cards are taken from the language support pack (6 cards per set, 6 sets, laminated), which replaces the Week 1 kit card's 'set of 5'.

Language support pack items (classroom language cards, A3 posters, role cards, My Science Dictionary) come from the Teacher Guide prep calendar, Before Week 1 (language pass), All years row. They apply to Year 7. The printables file (1 card per student plus 6 spares) takes priority over the prep calendar (1 per student).

Foil troughs replace the 'moulds' and 'ice-lolly moulds or ice-cube trays' named in the Teacher Guide (Before Week 1 and Week 6 rows) and in Outline Section 11. The trough template block can be a wood offcut or a stack of rulers taped together (Week 7 kit card). The wood offcut is listed as its own ingredient; use rulers and masking tape if no wood is to hand.

Classroom furniture and services are not listed either: desks for the rigs, a wall clock, sinks and soap for hand-washing (Plan B, Weeks 7 and 8), bins and recycling bins, the on-screen timer, a laminator and a guillotine or trimmer for cutting card sets. open_questions: Freezer decision by Week 4: Plan A (ice) or Plan B (no freezer). This decides most of the Week 6 to 8 kit (ice, gloves, cool boxes, freezer drawer versus thermometers, kettle, flour, salt, dry shelf).

Thermometers: does the prep room have 7 spirit or digital thermometers for Week 6 Plan B? Count them in Week 1.
Week 7 approved plans: which question and samples each group chooses, and how many choose the melting test (Plan A, at most 2). This sets the fibre amounts and the Week 8 melting kit.
Trial result: 5 mm strips, thinner 3 to 4 mm strips, or an 8 cm span? This changes the water, dough and fibre amounts and the rig.
Footprint puzzle cards: print on card (18 sheets) or laminate (18 A4 pouches)?
Week 4 spare spinner card: print the 9 reserve sheets the print spec asks for, or only the 3 the kit card puts on the teacher desk?

Week 8 cloth towels (13): where will they come from?

Week 8 Hook: the kit card says 2 spare plain strips, but the slide notes say to hold up a plain strip and a fibre strip. Should a group's spare (tenth) trough be used for a fibre strip?

Allergy list: which students have a wheat or flour allergy (Plan B Weeks 7 and 8)? Arrange non-dough roles for them.
Laminating: does the school have a laminator, and who will laminate the language cards, role cards, data cards, rig diagrams and A3 boards?

assumptions: One class of 24 students in 6 groups of 4, one lesson a week. Every quantity is for one class; multiply for more classes.
For reusable items (goggles, cups, rulers, magnifiers, pens), the amount to buy or borrow is the largest single-week figure, not the sum of the weeks.

Weeks 7 and 8: each group's option (Soil, Paper, Ink 2, Powder 2) is chosen from the Week 6 exit tickets, with every option done by at least one group and no option by more than two. Week 7 and Week 8 quantities allow for the maximum of two groups on every option, which adds up to 8 groups' worth of kit; reduce them once the allocation is known.
Where a card says 'paper towels' or 'a few' with no number, 3 sheets per group are assumed. 'Wipe tables' is costed as one damp cloth per group. Name cards are one per student.

Quantities follow the kit cards, because the Teacher Guide prep calendar says kit card quantities take priority. But the Case Bible header and Teacher Guide Section 9 say that where a lesson file disagrees with the Case Bible, the Case Bible wins. Three differences are therefore raised as open questions rather than settled: scene liquid (about 10 ml per group on the kit card, about 20 ml in the Case Bible), the Evidence 6 container (sealed bag on the kit card, labelled jar in the Case Bible and prep calendar), and pens (one set per group on the kit card, two of each brand in the Case Bible and prep calendar).

No file gives a recipe for the baking soda solution. 2 level teaspoons in about 100 ml of water are allowed for Week 5. The files do not give the amount of vinegar and salt water for the teacher's Ink 2 pre-test either; small amounts are noted rather than counted.
Powders and liquids are left in the units the cards use (teaspoons, ml). Coffee filters are counted as 2 cm by 10 cm strips; how many filters that means depends on the filter size.

Only special print stock is listed: card, lamination, colour, A3, envelopes and the photo print. Ordinary printing goes to reprographics and is left out. This covers worksheets, slides, skills checks, surveys, checkpoint papers, logbooks and My Science Dictionary booklets. It also covers the case file inner pages, the Fingerprint File and its display copy, the Teacher Pre-test Record, plan sheets, the Week 8 kit card copies, recording sheets and backup lab report cards. The sentence frame bank (A4 poster and 6 A6 card sets), the cleaning log cards, the concept cartoon, expert witness badges, reveal cards, jury notes, run sheets and the talk record are ordinary prints too, as are self-assessment and peer feedback slips, the final case file checklist, height station signs, the A5 'Evidence: do not touch' sign and the Ideas Parking Board header. The scene footprint is listed because it is a kit card item that must be printed at exactly 100%.

The language support pack is included in Week 1 because the Teacher Guide prep calendar lists it for all years before Week 1. That means 30 laminated A5 classroom language cards, 6 laminated A4 sheets of role cards (laminated as sheets, then cut) and 3 A3 posters per room. One version serves Years 7 and 8.
The enlarged A3 pH chart for the wall is assumed to be printed in colour. The 'enlarged' teacher-model evidence board is counted as one A3 sheet because no size is given.

The teacher's demonstrations in Weeks 2, 3 and 4 use one group's kit, because those cards name no extra demo kit. The Week 5 Hook demo (2 indicator cups, vinegar, baking soda solution) and the Week 6 Hook metre stick are added.
Plastic cups are treated as reusable because the Week 5 card says to rinse them for reuse or recycle them.

These are assumed to be in the room already and are not listed: projector and screen, a visualiser for the Week 2 demonstration, and the board and board pens. So are the teacher's phone or a school camera for photographs, tap water, a sink with soap for hand-washing, wall space for the Ideas Parking Board and a windowsill for the soil bottles. The teacher's clipboard (named in the Week 8 and Week 10 run sheet specs) and a stapler (the final case file checklist is stapled inside each case file) are also assumed. Photographs are needed of the note, the Ideas Parking Board, the Week 8 results and the Week 9 boards.

The Case Bible says to chop the cabbage and grate the soap, so a knife, chopping board and grater from the kitchen are assumed. The teacher's own scissors or a guillotine are assumed for cutting filter strips, card packs, jury cards and the cleaning log label strips. None of these is listed.
Year 8 needs no freezer, so every item is marked 'both'. The only freezer use is the optional frosty notebook prop in Week 10.

The Programme Outline Section 11 list was used only as a cross-check, and the kit cards take priority. The kit cards ask for more droppers (36 in Week 5 against 12) and more iodine (6 dropper bottles in Week 4 against 1 small bottle). The outline lists rulers for Week 2 and scissors for Week 3, but those kit cards do not; the kit card figures are used.

Week 7: the kit card gives every Powder 2 group a sealed Evidence 3 bag. The Week 4 bags will usually have been opened during testing, so 2 new zip bags, 2 labels and about 3 teaspoons of baking soda per bag (the Week 4 amount) are counted. Skip them if unopened Week 4 bags are left. Week 7 labels therefore rise to 6 and zip bags to 6.
Week 7: the N strips shown to Ink 2 groups in clear sleeves are counted as 2 new coffee-filter strips. The 2 spare N strips from Week 3 can be used instead.
Week 3 'Sticky tape or paper clips, a few': both are listed. Paper clips are counted at 5 per group (one per strip) and are needed only if tape is not used.
The Week 4 Do Now says students 'stick chromatograms in the Week 3 worksheet box' but names no adhesive. The clear tape already in the trays is assumed.
Week 8 Ink 2 teacher pre-test: following Case Bible Section 11 (one strip per cup), 6 cups are counted. 'Fill the vinegar bottle' is counted as one small bottle per Ink 2 group.
Teacher teaspoon rows (Week 4 powders, Week 8 mixtures) are a measuring spoon for amounts the cards give in teaspoons. Only the Ink 2 teaspoon is named as kit on a card.
open_questions: Pens A to D: buy 6 full sets (24 pens), one set per group as the Week 3 kit card asks? Or buy only two of each brand (8 pens, as the Case Bible and the prep calendar say) and pre-dot strips A to D for every group yourself, which adds 10 minutes? If two brands look too similar in the pre-test, you will need a fifth brand.

assumptions: Class of 24 in 6 groups of 4. 'Per group' quantities are multiplied by 6, 'per pair' by 12 and 'per student' by 24. Teacher items and any spares a card gives a number for are added. Where a card mentions spares without a number (gloves, goggles, thermometers and paper towels in Week 8, gloves in Week 6, talk frame cards), only the named quantity is counted.

Week 8 claim kits depend on which claims groups choose in Week 7 (up to 2 groups per claim; check the approval-slip stubs). For each claim item, the Week 8 quantity assumes that every claim using it is run by one group. That gives a planning figure: double a claim's share if two groups choose it, and drop claims nobody chose. Only 6 claims can run, so figures for items shared by several claims will usually be too high. The items on every tray (pens, stopwatch, tray, paper towels, data-quality checklist) are true class totals.

Ice: Week 6 uses the top of the 2 to 3 kg range. Week 8 is about 1 kg per ice-claim group, so 4 kg if one group takes each of claims 1, 2, 5 and 6, and up to 6 kg if all six groups pick ice claims. All ice is Plan A only and collected on the day, so Year 9 needs no freezer space of its own.

Salt for Week 8 (0.5 kg) is an estimate; the cards just say 'salt'. The claim 1 freezing mixture is about 3 parts ice to 1 part salt, claim 2 uses about 1 tablespoon per 200 ml cup of salt water, and claim 5 sprinkles salt on cubes. What is left of the Week 6 1 kg bag may be enough.
Paper towels '1 each' per group is read as one supply per group per practical lesson. One or two kitchen rolls per practical lesson is a guess.
Week 9 'pencils and pens: 4' per group is read as 4 of each.
The pens are listed as one item: the 24 identical Week 5 pens are reused for raw data in Week 8 and in Week 9. The Week 8 teacher kit also names 'a pen' for the run sheet, so Week 8 is 25.

Numbers not given on the Week 8 tray labels were assumed: 2 pencils for claim 8 (one per stopwatch), 6 sticky notes for claim 9 (as for one Week 4 group), 10 sheets of A4 for claim 9 (one per volunteer; the run sheet says 10 or more people), and 3 rubber bands for claim 3 (one per fabric piece).

Claim 6 in Week 8 needs 300 g of crushed ice that the teacher crushes, but no Week 7 or Week 8 card says how. The Week 6 method (a clean bag and a rolling pin) is assumed, so those two items have a Week 8 row.

Envelopes are marked reusable. The Week 1 and Week 4 card sets keep their envelopes, and the Week 2 slip envelopes could be reused for the Week 7 claim bank sets. The smallest number you could buy is about 8 (6 for card sets plus 2 A4-size for Week 10).

Plastic cups: claims 4 and 6 put 200 ml of water in a cup, so cups that hold at least 250 ml are safer for Week 8. In Week 6, 12 cups covers Plan B; Plan A needs 6, more if you nest cups or have no tube rack.
Thermometers: 12 in Week 6 (2 per group) plus 1 teacher spare. If the prep room has only 6, use the single-tube or single-cup method on the Week 6 kit card.
